title: A Ledger for the Will
premise: Mara Ravensworth, the unassuming archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years solving the deaths the police dismissed, keeping their gift hidden behind ledgers and dust. When a drowned man is found wearing clothes stolen from Mara's own closet—clothes only one person could have taken—the city's most dangerous family realizes the archivist who ruined them three times is still alive. The trail leads to Verity Ashcombe, the witness who testified against the Ashcombes twenty years ago, officially dead and buried in the cathedral's locked crypt. As Mara races to find Verity before the killers do, they uncover that Verity never died at all: she became the crypt's secret keeper, and her ledger of confessions names every corrupt hand in the city—including Mara's own late mother. In the end, Mara must choose between exposing the ledger and destroying the last proof of who their mother truly was; they choose justice, the crypt opens, and the price of survival is finally paid by those who set it.
about_author: Freya Okonkwo spent a decade cataloguing parish records in northern England before turning to crime fiction, a career that taught her that every archive hides a body. She writes from a converted vestry office, where she keeps an unopened ledger on her desk as a reminder that some accounts are never settled.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man Wearing My Coat
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A body pulled from the millrace wears clothes stolen from Mara's own wardrobe, down to a monogrammed shirt no thief should know exists. The police call it accidental drowning; Mara recognizes the staging instantly. Emotional beat: cold dread—the invisibility Mara built for fifteen years has been pierced deliberately.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Hand
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with flashbacks. Mara reviews the three deaths they quietly solved: the fall from the bell tower, the fire at the almshouse, the poisoned communion wine—all traced to the Ashcombe family's fixer, Denny Vole. Now someone is killing in Mara's pattern. Beat: the hunter realizes they've become the template.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The locked crypt beneath St. Aldhelm's holds tombs of the Ashcombe founders—and one empty coffin belonging to Verity Ashcombe, declared dead in 1999 after testifying against her own family. Mara finds fresh candle wax inside. Beat: hope sharpened into urgency—someone visits the dead woman's grave.

chapters.title: Inspector Halloway Suspects
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. The detective who once nearly caught Mara notices the drowned man's clothes match a missing-persons report filed under a false name—one only the archivist would use. He doesn't accuse; he watches. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension, the law circling closer than the killers know.

chapters.title: Ledger Entries, Mother's Hand
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Cataloguing old parish donations, Mara recognizes their dead mother's handwriting in payments to 'V.A., custodial services' spanning two decades. Their mother was paying someone to stay buried. Beat: grief curdling into betrayal—the parent Mara mourned was complicit.

chapters.title: Denny Vole Comes to Dust the Books
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Vole visits the archive under pretense of researching family history, asking pointed questions about the crypt and complimenting Mara's memory. Mara plays the timid clerk while noting Vole's shoes are wet with river silt. Beat: quiet terror performed as boredom; survival as theater.

chapters.title: The Witness Everyone Swears Is Dead
chapters.summary: Verity's POV (first appearance). An old woman living in the sealed passages between crypt and cloister tends candles over her own grave. She knows someone has been reading her traces, and she knows the Ashcombes have found a new archivist to hunt. Beat: wary loneliness; she has survived by being no one.

chapters.title: A Name in the Confession Book
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the wax trail through a disused stair, Mara finds Verity's hiding place: a confession ledger naming every official the Ashcombes bought, including the coroner who certified Verity's death—and Mara's mother, who laundered the bribes. Beat: vertigo; the truth is a debt with Mara's name in the margin.

chapters.title: Twenty Years in the Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara/Verity. Verity explains why she faked her death: testifying got her sister killed, so she let herself be buried alive in paperwork and stayed to guard the ledger. She refuses to give it up. Beat: two survivors negotiating trust across a candlelit table.

chapters.title: Halloway Finds the Second Body
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. A cathedral verger who helped stage the drowning is found hanged, staged like Mara's second solved case. Halloway realizes the killer is framing the archivist—and that means the archivist is real, and brilliant. Beat: reluctant respect warring with duty.

chapters.title: The Ashcombes' Reckoning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Patriarch Edmund Ashcombe learns the ledger still exists and orders Vole to burn the crypt 'with whatever lives in it.' His daughter Camille hesitates—she remembers Aunt Verity's kindness. Beat: rot at the top; even monsters have cracks.

chapters.title: Fire in the Lower Dark
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Smoke floods the crypt passages; Mara drags Verity out through the ossuary as the confession room burns. The original ledger is destroyed—but Mara memorized key pages during their meeting. Beat: loss and fury; the archive keeper watching archives burn.

chapters.title: Framed
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Evidence implicates Mara in both murders: the stolen clothes, the verger's appointment book with Mara's forged signature. Halloway arrests the archivist but privately doubts the neatness of it all. Beat: the trap closing; justice and law pulling apart.

chapters.title: Camille's Doubt
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. Searching her father's study for answers, Camille finds her aunt's death certificate with mismatched ink and a photograph of Verity holding baby Camille. She begins quietly sabotaging Vole. Beat: inherited guilt becoming chosen defiance.

chapters.title: The Cell and the Cipher
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, in custody. Mara deciphers a message smuggled in a hymnal from Verity: a backup copy of the ledger exists where 'the dead keep their appointments.' Mara must escape or guide Halloway there. Beat: patience weaponized; the archivist's mind as the last safe.

chapters.title: Where the Dead Keep Their Appointments
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Verity retrieves the duplicate ledger from the columbarium, hidden inside her sister's urn—the one thing the Ashcombes would never disturb. Vole follows her. Beat: dread rising; the past literally in ashes, guarded by the living dead.

chapters.title: Halloway Breaks His Own Case
chapters.summary: Halloway's POV. Comparing the frame-up evidence against Mara's known methods, Halloway finds the forgery too perfect—only someone with access to police files could have built it. He releases Mara and offers an uneasy alliance. Beat: the law choosing conscience over procedure.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Columbarium
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Vole corners Verity among the urns; Mara and Halloway arrive as Edmund Ashcombe himself appears to burn the ledger personally. Camille turns on her father. In the struggle, Vole falls into the crypt shaft; Edmund is arrested with the ledger open in his hands. Beat: violent catharsis; every debt called at once.

chapters.title: The Testimony of a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Verity's POV. Legally resurrected, Verity gives sworn testimony that dismantles the Ashcombe empire. She asks Mara why they kept solving deaths no one asked about. Mara answers: because someone has to keep the record honest. Beat: weary vindication; justice outside the law finally entering it.

chapters.title: My Mother's Page
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Alone with the recovered ledger, Mara reads their mother's final entry—a payment marked not as bribe but as penance, funding Verity's survival for twenty years. Grief refracts: complicity and love in the same handwriting. Beat: sorrow without absolution; the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Opening the Crypt
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The cathedral unlocks the crypt for the first time in a generation; sunlight reaches the empty coffin, now bearing Verity's true dates—two death dates, one life. Mara files the confession ledger into the public archive. Beat: release; secrets surrendered to light.

chapters.title: A Ledger for the Will
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, epilogue. Halloway leaves a new case file on the archive desk—an 'accident' that isn't—and walks away without a word. Mara opens a fresh ledger and writes the first line. Beat: quiet resolve; the invisible archivist chooses, at last, to be seen.
